messages.content: Write the opening pitch section of a README for a new open source charting library. Around 200 words.

output:
Passes the slopwatch gate clean. ~205 words:

---

# Axil

Axil draws charts from data you already have, in about as much code as it takes to describe the chart out loud.

Most charting libraries make you pick a side. Either you get a handful of preset chart types behind a config object, and you are stuck the moment a design brief asks for something the presets do not cover, or you get a grammar of graphics that can draw anything and takes a weekend to learn.

Axil starts with the presets and lets you drop a level when you need to. A bar chart is one call. Adding a second y-axis, a custom tick formatter, or an annotation layer over that same bar chart does not mean rewriting it as a scale-and-mark composition: the preset hands back the same objects the low-level API operates on.

It renders to SVG, has no runtime dependencies, and weighs about 14 kB gzipped for the core plus whatever chart types you import. Axes and legends are accessible without configuration, using real text nodes, keyboard-reachable, with a data table fallback for screen readers.

Written in TypeScript, MIT licensed, and usable from React, Vue, Svelte, or a bare DOM node.
